M.name: Fan body (motor head, stand and control housing)
M.look: largest part: motor housing on a short column, with 4 push buttons (0 1 2 3) at the bottom

B.name: Round base
B.look: flat round disc with a notch or marker at the front

C.name: Rear guard
C.look: round wire guard with a large centre hole, a plastic mounting plate and clips on its rim

F.name: Guard nut
F.look: large ribbed plastic ring, comes screwed onto the front of the motor

E.name: Spinner cap
E.look: small domed ribbed cap that screws onto the motor shaft

G.name: Front guard
G.look: domed wire guard with spiral wires and a badge in the middle

H.name: Guard clamp screw
H.look: small cross-head screw at the bottom of the guard rim

steps.title: Fit the rear guard
steps.text: Unscrew the plastic guard nut from the front of the motor. Slide the rear guard onto the motor so its holes fit over the pins and the handle or ribs point down.
steps.tip: Check that all the pins sit in their holes before going on.

steps.title: Tighten the guard nut
steps.text: Screw the guard nut back onto the motor, turning it clockwise until the rear guard is held firmly.

steps.title: Push on the blade
steps.text: Push the fan blade onto the motor shaft as far as it goes.
steps.tip: Line up the flat side of the shaft with the slot in the blade hub.

steps.title: Screw on the spinner cap
steps.text: Screw the spinner cap onto the shaft in the direction of the arrow (anticlockwise seen from the front) until it is tight.
steps.tip: The cap usually has a reverse thread: turning it clockwise loosens it.

steps.title: Put on the front guard
steps.text: Open the clips on the rim of the rear guard. Hook the top of the front guard onto the rear guard, with the badge upright, and press it onto the rim.
steps.tip: Keep the badge level so the guard is not fitted crooked.

steps.title: Tighten the bottom screw
steps.text: Tighten the screw at the bottom of the guard rim with a Phillips screwdriver.

steps.title: Close the clips
steps.text: Fold all the clips over the front guard rim until they snap shut.
steps.tip: Turn the blade by hand: it must not touch either guard.

steps.title: Attach the base
steps.text: Set the fan body onto the round base, line up the mark on the body with the notch on the base and press it down until it locks.

steps.title: Set oscillation
steps.text: Push the knob on top of the motor down to make the fan swing from side to side. Pull it up to stop the swinging.

steps.title: Adjust the tilt
steps.text: Tilt the fan head up or down by hand to aim the air.

steps.title: Plug in
steps.text: Put the plug into a wall socket.
steps.warn: Only plug in once the fan is fully assembled with both guards closed.

steps.title: Choose a speed
steps.text: Press button 1, 2 or 3 for low, medium or high speed. Press 0 to switch off.

steps.title: Unplug after use
steps.text: Switch off with button 0 and pull the plug out of the socket before moving or cleaning the fan.
steps.warn: Always unplug before cleaning or taking the guards off.
